editorial.headline: Interior Design With Room for Full Foreign Ownership
editorial.standfirst: KBLI 74191 frames interior design as a full professional service—shaping spaces around use, safety, health, comfort, accessibility and atmosphere, from study to supervision.
editorial.body:
KBLI 74191 treats interior design as the disciplined shaping of the inside of a building around the way people use it. The work begins with planning and designing rooms and interiors to suit human activity and the function of the space, but it seeks a particular atmosphere as well as an orderly plan. Safety, health, security, comfort, disability support and aesthetic considerations all sit within the stated scope. The activity therefore works at the point where a space must feel coherent while also responding to the practical demands placed on it. Rather than ending at a concept, it is defined by a considered interior response to use, function and atmosphere.

The category gives that proposition a broad professional envelope. It includes the design-consulting service itself, alongside survey work, feasibility studies, drafting, artistic-impression design, supervision of building interiors, price estimation/QS and project management within the construction planning of an interior-design project. It reaches interiors in buildings as well as other civil structures. In registration terms, the activity is open at Mikro, Kecil, Menengah and Besar scales. The business being registered is thus one that supplies interior-design consulting and design services, whether its role remains in planning or includes the supporting work specified for an interior-design project.

Nationally, the PMA status is open, with a maximum foreign ownership ceiling of 100%. That is a full foreign-ownership position for this activity, not a ceiling below complete ownership. Its cited PMA basis is Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021. The national position sits over the whole stated scope: planning and designing interiors, and the related survey, feasibility, drafting, artistic-impression, supervision, estimation and project-management services. It is a national setting that reflects the category’s comprehensive account of interior-design work.

Bali calls for a separate reading, and the result remains open on the facts given. The island-wide, permanent moratorium blocks PMA activity classified at Low or Medium-Low risk. This activity is expressly not blocked by that moratorium. At the Besar scale, its OSS risk is recorded as Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi—Medium-High/High—which places it in Bali’s OK-or-higher-risk position. The distinction matters because the national openness is not cancelled in Bali by the rule supplied here. The honest conclusion is straightforward: a foreign investor may register this interior-design activity in Bali today, with national foreign ownership open up to 100% and its large-scale risk classification outside the stated PMA moratorium.
